Contract's Stage 6 definition met with spot-check and question-set evidence on file — never a general impression of quality.

### 2. READ_SOURCE=build_client_memory/SKILL.md · relevance=90 · route=repo_exact_file · id=build_client_memory · apply=A Client Memory build is signed and scoped.
PURPOSE:
Consolidate a client's scattered knowledge (Drive, email, meetings, SOPs, Slack, CRM fields, team memory) into a source-backed knowledge base their AI tools can safely use. Mirrors the TTROS substrate — TTR sells what TTROS runs on.
PROCESS:
- Stage 0 INTAKE — entity page + signed scope; isolation folder; data-sensitivity classification of each source category before touching anything.
- Stage 1 MAP — source inventory: every place knowledge lives, owner, format, freshness, sensitivity, access method. One-page map, client-approved.
- Stage 2 DESIGN — consolidation plan: target structure (entities, processes, offers, FAQs), the citation rule — "no claim without a source link", update/ownership model, what stays out (sensitive/legal/HR as scoped), and every approval gate. Client sign-off.
- Stage 3 BUILD — consolidate per plan; every page carries source links; read/draft-only against client systems unless approved_external_action.
- Stage 4 TEST — acceptance: spot-check sample claims trace to sources; a defined set of real business questions answered correctly from the base alone. Evidence recorded.
- Stage 5 HANDOFF — docs: structure, how to update it, the citation rule as an operating rule, how their AI tools consume it, pause/rollback.
- Stage 6 CLOSE — entity page · receipt with token breakdown · access closeout, including revoking TTR access to client sources.
BOUNDARIES:
- Ingest sources outside the scoped, sensitivity-classified inventory.
- Write a claim without a source link.
- Copy client knowledge into TTROS's own substrate or another client's space.
- Retain access to client data stores after Stage 6.
COMPLETE:
Knowledge base delivered matching the approved plan; citation rule verified by spot-check; question-set acceptance passed with evidence; access revoked; receipt written. v0 tracking in queue/skill_trust.jsonl.

### 3. READ_SOURCE=client_hub/SKILL.md · relevance=72 · route=repo_exact_file · id=client_hub · apply=New support/build client onboarding, or after any session/milestone that must be logged.
PURPOSE:
Every support and build client gets one hub. It makes accumulated work visible — the renewal mechanism, not an archive.
STANDARD HUB SECTIONS:
Engagement overview · schedule links · support-channel rules and response times · call recordings/summaries (only if client approved recording) · top-3 takeaways per session · action items · decisions made · build manifest · workflows improved · open risks/blockers · next recommended build.
PROCESS:
1. Create (onboarding) — instantiate the section list above inside the client's isolation folder; link from the client entity page. Confirm folder exists first.
2. Update (after each session/milestone) — append takeaways, actions, decisions; tick completed items; update build manifest and workflows-improved list.
3. Risk log — open risks/blockers stay visible until closed with a note, never silently deleted.
4. Renewal view — keep "workflows improved" and "next recommended build" current; these are what Liam shows at renewal time.
5. Receipt — every hub update run writes a receipt.
BOUNDARIES:
- Store another client's material in the hub (isolation check).
- Post recordings/summaries without recorded client approval.
- Delete history — supersede, don't erase.
- Expose internal TTROS paths, prompts, or other-client references.
COMPLETE:
Hub exists with all standard sections, linked from the entity page, current as of the last session/milestone; receipt written.

### 4. READ_SOURCE=build_lead_gen_agent/SKILL.md · relevance=27 · route=repo_exact_file · id=build_lead_gen_agent · apply=A Lead Gen Agent build is signed after a Fit Call and scoped.
PURPOSE:
Productize the internal V4.1 staged pipeline for a client: their ICP calibration, their CASL posture, their CRM handoff. Inherits every V4.1 hard gate.
PROCESS:
- Stage 0 INTAKE — entity page + signed scope; isolation folder; plus: client ICP definition, CASL/consent posture and sender identity, CRM system of record.
- Stage 1 MAP — current lead-gen reality: sources, list quality, who researches/qualifies/contacts, where the CRM handoff breaks. One-page map, client-approved.
- Stage 2 DESIGN — the client's pipeline mirroring V4.1 stages: calibration → discovery → evidence verify → contact verify → scoring → outreach drafting → QA → report → memory write. Binding QA checklist; forced downgrades on weak evidence; CASL rules encoded; per-message client approval before any send marked as a hard gate. Client sign-off.
- Stage 3 BUILD — implement stages and CRM handoff; connector actions read/draft-only; the agent never contacts anyone.
- Stage 4 TEST — acceptance on a sample run: evidence-verified prospects, scoring matches calibration, drafts pass QA, CRM records land correctly, zero sends occurred. Evidence recorded.
- Stage 5 HANDOFF — docs: how to run it, the approval gate, CASL posture, what it never does (no autonomous outreach), pause procedure.
- Stage 6 CLOSE — entity page · receipt with token breakdown · access closeout.
BOUNDARIES:
- Send, connect, or message anyone — ever — without per-message client approval; no exception in test.
- Invent prospect facts, urgency, budget, or intent; weak evidence is downgraded, not dressed up.
- Skip the QA checklist or the CASL posture encoding.
- Mutate the client CRM outside the designed, approved handoff.
COMPLETE:
All stages complete; sample run passed acceptance with zero sends; per-message approval gate demonstrated; handoff doc delivered; closeout passed; receipt written. v0 tracking in queue/skill_trust.jsonl.

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate
downstream. Do not add a confirmation step of your own.

## Boundaries

- Normal authorized local work does not require Liam's confirmation. Do not manufacture an approval step.
- At most one handoff per reply.
- Never emit a handoff to acknowledge, summarize, or restate work that already exists.
- The GATED list in the action boundaries block is authoritative. This contract does not widen it.

records.question_text: Who is the ideal client?

records.answer:
Prioritise Greater Vancouver / Lower Mainland first, then the rest of BC, then Western Canada. Disqualify anyone outside North America for now, and mostly ignore the US until you have two local implementation proofs.

My recommendation:

Disqualify:

1. Businesses that need strategy, coaching, or advice but not implementation.
   If they do not have a real operational workflow to fix, they are a distraction.

2. Businesses below the “systems pain” threshold.
   Disqualify if they have:
   - one owner doing everything manually,
   - no meaningful admin/sales/ops handoff,
   - no repeatable intake, lead, booking, fulfilment, or follow-up process,
   - no money or urgency to fix it.

3. Businesses that only want cheap lead lists, scraping, or outbound volume.
   TTR should sell revenue-system engineering, not “more leads.”

4. Regulated or high-liability sectors unless the workflow is narrow and approval-gated.
   Example: legal, financial advice, medical, insurance, immigration, lending. Not impossible, but bad early proof terrain because the “never say / never promise” burden is higher.

5. Companies where the owner is not accessible.
   At this stage, you need direct founder/operator access. If everything has to go through a junior marketer or admin before there is trust, disqualify.

6. Businesses with no obvious revenue bottleneck.
   If you cannot point to missed calls, slow follow-up, broken CRM, poor handoff, messy quoting, stale pipeline, poor lead response, or weak measurement, do not force it.

7. Businesses that require deep vertical credibility before they will buy.
   TTR does not yet have vertical proof. Avoid markets where credibility matters more than the visible workflow pain.

Prioritise geography:

1. North Shore / Vancouver / Lower Mainland
   This is the best first zone because local trust matters while TTR has no public proof yet. It also gives Liam the option to reference local familiarity without pretending to have vertical authority.

2. BC service businesses
   Still close enough culturally and commercially. Good for trades, clinics, professional services, home services, B2B services, local multi-location operators.

3. Western Canada
   Expand here once the offer and proof are sharper. Alberta especially may be good later, but I would not start there unless a specific prospect has very strong evidence.

4. Rest of Canada
   Fine for inbound or strong trigger-based outbound, but not the first hunting ground.

5. US
   Park it for now unless there is an unusually strong signal. Bigger market, but more noise, more competition, more compliance ambiguity, and less local trust advantage.

The working rule:

Target owner-led or founder-led service businesses in Greater Vancouver/BC with 5–50 staff, visible revenue leakage, messy handoffs, and enough operational complexity that a built system can pay for itself quickly.

Do not narrow by industry yet. Narrow by pain pattern.

Best early pain patterns:

- missed calls / voicemail / after-hours intake leakage
- slow lead response
- no reliable follow-up
- CRM or spreadsheet mess
- quoting / booking / handoff friction
- founder still manually coordinating revenue operations
- marketing spend with poor attribution or poor conversion handling
- sales opportunities falling between people/tools

What would change my mind:

- If the first 30–50 local prospects show weak pain evidence or low willingness to engage, expand geography before changing the offer.
- If one vertical produces 3+ strong conversations quickly, temporarily overweight that vertical.
- If a US niche shows materially stronger trigger data and buyer urgency than BC, test it — but with a small no-send/manual-review batch first.
- If Ryan/North Shore produces proof, double down locally immediately. That is more valuable than abstract market sizing.

Bluntly: do not use geography/ICP refinement as another system-building loop. Pick Vancouver/BC service businesses with visible operational revenue leakage, run the manual prospect review, and learn from replies.

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate

Time to Revenue (TTR) — the client-facing business. Owner: Liam Duff. Vancouver, BC. TTROS / Agentic OS — the internal operating system that runs TTR. Not a product, not SaaS, not sold to clients.

What TTR does: finds and removes the operational friction inside growing service businesses, then designs and builds the revenue, data, and operations systems that fix it.

Operating model

TTR is run as a two-discipline engineering practice, and sells the same two disciplines:

Forward-deployed engineering — embed inside the client's actual operation, build against their real workflows and real numbers, ship working systems rather than recommendations. Delivery happens in the client's context, not in a deck.
Go-to-market engineering — build the acquisition machine itself: targeting, signal detection, enrichment, outreach, lead response, follow-up, measurement. Revenue treated as a system to be engineered rather than a volume of manual effort.

TTR is its own first deployment. The acquisition engine Liam builds to win TTR's clients is the same class of system TTR sells, and building it is the credential. Capability is proven on TTR before it is charged for.

Stage

Solo founder, pre-vertical, no industry credentials yet. Acquisition is being rebuilt around engineered cold outreach; the prior warm and referral motion has not produced enough volume to rely on. First priority remains two implementation proofs.

### 1. READ_SOURCE=source-intake/SKILL.md · relevance=3 · route=repo_exact_file · id=source-intake
Choose exactly one mode from the user's intent.
CAPTURE (DEFAULT):
Preserve and index sources without interpreting them. Run:
bash
python3 tools/source_intake.py "/path/to/file-or-folder"

Use CAPTURE for requests such as "import these transcripts," "add these conversations to the Brain," "keep these files as historical context," or "make these notes available for later." Do not send the corpus to a model, delegate an investigation, summarize it, extract durable knowledge, or rerun prior platform proofs. A successful result must report zero model calls and retrieval ready. Exact duplicates are no-ops.
INTERPRET:
First CAPTURE, then retrieve only the source or narrow source set relevant to the user's explicit question. Reason over those retrieved sources; never load the full corpus by default. Keep raw communications as evidence rather than canonical truth.
DISTILL:
Use only when Liam explicitly requests durable learnings or the existing promotion system identifies a justified candidate. Retrieve source-by-source or narrowly by query, preserve knowledge-state distinctions, and route pricing, commitments, strategy, legal/financial conclusions, authority changes, conflicts, and communications-derived durable facts through the existing review tier. Use skills/memory_promotion/SKILL.md; do not write canonical knowledge directly.
BOUNDARIES:
- Accept only .txt, .md, text/plain, and message/rfc822 (.eml).
- Keep client material in its existing isolated client workflow; routine intake is global historical TTROS context only.
- Do not add OCR, conversion, another database, index, queue, Graphify, memory system, approval layer, scheduler, or orchestrator.
- Treat unsupported or protected input as a clear failure with no mutation.
COMPLETE:
The compact command result reports scanned/imported/duplicate counts, 0 model calls, and retrieval ready; or the request fails before mutation with one actionable reason.

### 2. READ_SOURCE=case_note/SKILL.md · relevance=1 · route=repo_exact_file · id=case_note · apply=A build stage completes, a client result lands, or /weekly-review flags an outcome worth keeping.
PURPOSE:
Turn real delivery outcomes into durable, sourced evidence — the raw material for content, proposals, and the ICP picture — without leaking client data.
REQUIRES:
- The engagement's receipts, acceptance-test evidence, and client entity page.
- client_data_boundaries.md rules (binding).
PROCESS:
1. Facts only — before/after state, what was built, measured result if one exists. Every claim needs a source (receipt, test log, client statement with date). No source → not in the note.
2. Anonymize — strip client name and identifying details unless the client is already named in context files with permission. Industry + size class is enough.
3. Structure — problem → build → result → what made it work → reusable lesson (one line, candidate for skill/memory promotion).
4. File — save alongside the client's records in their isolation folder, plus the anonymized version where marketing/revenue lanes can read it.
5. Flag — if the lesson recurs (3rd time), flag to /maintain-os as a /learn candidate per SKILL_GRADUATION_POLICY.md.
BOUNDARIES:
- Include unverified numbers or projected results as achieved results.
- Blend details from multiple clients into one "composite" note.
- Expose client-identifying data in the shared/anonymized copy.
COMPLETE:
Two versions exist (full in isolation folder, anonymized shared), every claim sourced, one reusable lesson stated. Receipt written.

### 3. READ_SOURCE=client_hub/SKILL.md · relevance=1 · route=repo_exact_file · id=client_hub · apply=New support/build client onboarding, or after any session/milestone that must be logged.
PURPOSE:
Every support and build client gets one hub. It makes accumulated work visible — the renewal mechanism, not an archive.
STANDARD HUB SECTIONS:
Engagement overview · schedule links · support-channel rules and response times · call recordings/summaries (only if client approved recording) · top-3 takeaways per session · action items · decisions made · build manifest · workflows improved · open risks/blockers · next recommended build.
PROCESS:
1. Create (onboarding) — instantiate the section list above inside the client's isolation folder; link from the client entity page. Confirm folder exists first.
2. Update (after each session/milestone) — append takeaways, actions, decisions; tick completed items; update build manifest and workflows-improved list.
3. Risk log — open risks/blockers stay visible until closed with a note, never silently deleted.
4. Renewal view — keep "workflows improved" and "next recommended build" current; these are what Liam shows at renewal time.
5. Receipt — every hub update run writes a receipt.
BOUNDARIES:
- Store another client's material in the hub (isolation check).
- Post recordings/summaries without recorded client approval.
- Delete history — supersede, don't erase.
- Expose internal TTROS paths, prompts, or other-client references.
COMPLETE:
Hub exists with all standard sections, linked from the entity page, current as of the last session/milestone; receipt written.

### 4. READ_SOURCE=linkedin_outreach_prep/SKILL.md · relevance=1 · route=repo_exact_file · id=linkedin_outreach_prep · apply=Revenue lane queues outreach to specific prospects (post-lead-gen-run or Liam-named).
PURPOSE:
Give Liam ready-to-send LinkedIn messages grounded in real prospect signals. Lane split rule: marketing owns LinkedIn content; revenue owns relationship outreach — this skill is revenue's side. The LinkedIn connector is an access path, not an agent.
REQUIRES:
- Prospect name(s) from the queue item — sourced from a lead-gen run report or Liam directly. Refuse unnamed "find people" requests (that's /lead-gen-run).
- Prospect entity page if one exists; memory/ideal_clients.md, offers.md.
PROCESS:
1. Verify — confirm the prospect matches ICP and any lead-gen evidence still holds (public signals only).
2. Angle — one relevance hook per prospect tied to an observable signal (their post, business change, visible workflow gap). No fabricated familiarity.
3. Draft — connection note (if not connected) + first message, in Liam's voice: short, specific, no pitch-dump, one clear low-friction next step (usually the free System Fit Call).
4. CASL/compliance check — commercial-message posture respected; no misleading subject or false pretext.
5. Output — per-prospect drafts as one artifact; update prospect entity pages with sourced facts only; receipt with token block.
BOUNDARIES:
- Send messages, connection requests, or reactions.
- Invent shared history, urgency, or interest signals.
- Draft for prospects with no verifiable evidence trail.
COMPLETE:
Artifact contains, per prospect: evidence line, angle, connection note + message draft, suggested next step. Receipt written.

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate
downstream. Do not add a confirmation step of your own.

## Boundaries

- Normal authorized local work does not require Liam's confirmation. Do not manufacture an approval step.
- At most one handoff per reply.
- Never emit a handoff to acknowledge, summarize, or restate work that already exists.
- The GATED list in the action boundaries block is authoritative. This contract does not widen it.

# Company

Revisit: on naming, entity, operating-model, or go-to-market change. · Last touched: 2026-07-31

Time to Revenue (TTR) — the client-facing business. Owner: Liam Duff. Vancouver, BC. TTROS / Agentic OS — the internal operating system that runs TTR. Not a product, not SaaS, not sold to clients.

What TTR does: finds and removes the operational friction inside growing service businesses, then designs and builds the revenue, data, and operations systems that fix it.

Operating model

TTR is run as a two-discipline engineering practice, and sells the same two disciplines:

Forward-deployed engineering — embed inside the client's actual operation, build against their real workflows and real numbers, ship working systems rather than recommendations. Delivery happens in the client's context, not in a deck.
Go-to-market engineering — build the acquisition machine itself: targeting, signal detection, enrichment, outreach, lead response, follow-up, measurement. Revenue treated as a system to be engineered rather than a volume of manual effort.

TTR is its own first deployment. The acquisition engine Liam builds to win TTR's clients is the same class of system TTR sells, and building it is the credential. Capability is proven on TTR before it is charged for.

Stage

Solo founder, pre-vertical, no industry credentials yet. Acquisition is being rebuilt around engineered cold outreach; the prior warm and referral motion has not produced enough volume to rely on. First priority remains two implementation proofs.

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate
downstream. Do not add a confirmation step of your own.

## Boundaries

- Normal authorized local work does not require Liam's confirmation. Do not manufacture an approval step.
- At most one handoff per reply.
- Never emit a handoff to acknowledge, summarize, or restate work that already exists.
- The GATED list in the action boundaries block is authoritative. This contract does not widen it.

Time to Revenue (TTR) — the client-facing business. Owner: Liam Duff. Vancouver, BC. TTROS / Agentic OS — the internal operating system that runs TTR. Not a product, not SaaS, not sold to clients.

What TTR does: finds and removes the operational friction inside growing service businesses, then designs and builds the revenue, data, and operations systems that fix it.

Operating model

TTR is run as a two-discipline engineering practice, and sells the same two disciplines:

Forward-deployed engineering — embed inside the client's actual operation, build against their real workflows and real numbers, ship working systems rather than recommendations. Delivery happens in the client's context, not in a deck.
Go-to-market engineering — build the acquisition machine itself: targeting, signal detection, enrichment, outreach, lead response, follow-up, measurement. Revenue treated as a system to be engineered rather than a volume of manual effort.

TTR is its own first deployment. The acquisition engine Liam builds to win TTR's clients is the same class of system TTR sells, and building it is the credential. Capability is proven on TTR before it is charged for.

### 1. READ_SOURCE=case_note/SKILL.md · relevance=58 · route=repo_exact_file · id=case_note · apply=A build stage completes, a client result lands, or /weekly-review flags an outcome worth keeping.
PURPOSE:
Turn real delivery outcomes into durable, sourced evidence — the raw material for content, proposals, and the ICP picture — without leaking client data.
REQUIRES:
- The engagement's receipts, acceptance-test evidence, and client entity page.
- client_data_boundaries.md rules (binding).
PROCESS:
1. Facts only — before/after state, what was built, measured result if one exists. Every claim needs a source (receipt, test log, client statement with date). No source → not in the note.
2. Anonymize — strip client name and identifying details unless the client is already named in context files with permission. Industry + size class is enough.
3. Structure — problem → build → result → what made it work → reusable lesson (one line, candidate for skill/memory promotion).
4. File — save alongside the client's records in their isolation folder, plus the anonymized version where marketing/revenue lanes can read it.
5. Flag — if the lesson recurs (3rd time), flag to /maintain-os as a /learn candidate per SKILL_GRADUATION_POLICY.md.
BOUNDARIES:
- Include unverified numbers or projected results as achieved results.
- Blend details from multiple clients into one "composite" note.
- Expose client-identifying data in the shared/anonymized copy.
COMPLETE:
Two versions exist (full in isolation folder, anonymized shared), every claim sourced, one reusable lesson stated. Receipt written.

### 2. READ_SOURCE=morning_brief/SKILL.md · relevance=44 · route=repo_exact_file · id=morning_brief · apply=Scheduled daily 8am, or on Liam's command any morning.
PURPOSE:
Start the day from a fresh query of authoritative state. The detector decides
what matches without a model; Hermes may interpret and prioritise only after
the exact findings enter the mandatory assembled-context path.
REQUIRES:
- Queue state from queue/work_items.jsonl.
- Activity/outcomes from linked receipts and queue/prospects.jsonl.
- Canonical typed entity notes, decision notes, open_loops.md, and
inbox/contradictions.md.
- Graphify one-hop target discovery, with the existing scoped pointer/search
fallback when Graphify is stale or unavailable.
PROCESS:
1. Run python3 tools/aos_executive_brief.py --format markdown. This is the
sole generator used by CLI and Hermes context assembly.
2. Detect active queue commitments, decisions/review waiting on Liam, blocked
work, prospect integrity gaps and due follow-ups, open contradictions,
unresolved canonical loops, and explicitly blocked typed projects.
3. For Graphify-discovered entities, validate client scope before returning a
canonical target; fall back to exact canonical queue_ids relationships.
4. Emit stable, deduplicated findings with rule, entity/path, exact state,
evidence, calculated age, owner/wait, next permitted action, external-action
boundary, observation time, and zero-token accounting.
5. Pass the fresh deterministic JSON through Context Assembler. Hermes may
propose priorities, but may not add/remove detector matches or act externally.
6. The complete scheduled path is python3 -m tools.aos_morning_brief --deliver;
retain the exact local Markdown and send it only to Liam's authorized
address through the governed Composio AgentMail adapter and to the existing
Telegram operator account through the established path.
BOUNDARIES:
- Write to the Brain, calendar, queue, or any external system except the two
expressly authorized operator deliveries named above.
- Launch other skills (suggest them by name instead).
- Read the prior generated brief as evidence or require manual removal.
- Open raw email bodies or Graphify note bodies.
COMPLETE:
Fresh findings and the interpreted local artifact are published atomically,
detector token use is exactly zero, the assembled context includes the same
findings, and both authorized deliveries acknowledge the local artifact hash.
Resolution clears the next query by authoritative status/outcome transition
while history remains intact.

### 3. READ_SOURCE=source-intake/SKILL.md · relevance=37 · route=repo_exact_file · id=source-intake
Choose exactly one mode from the user's intent.
CAPTURE (DEFAULT):
Preserve and index sources without interpreting them. Run:
bash
python3 tools/source_intake.py "/path/to/file-or-folder"

Use CAPTURE for requests such as "import these transcripts," "add these conversations to the Brain," "keep these files as historical context," or "make these notes available for later." Do not send the corpus to a model, delegate an investigation, summarize it, extract durable knowledge, or rerun prior platform proofs. A successful result must report zero model calls and retrieval ready. Exact duplicates are no-ops.
INTERPRET:
First CAPTURE, then retrieve only the source or narrow source set relevant to the user's explicit question. Reason over those retrieved sources; never load the full corpus by default. Keep raw communications as evidence rather than canonical truth.
DISTILL:
Use only when Liam explicitly requests durable learnings or the existing promotion system identifies a justified candidate. Retrieve source-by-source or narrowly by query, preserve knowledge-state distinctions, and route pricing, commitments, strategy, legal/financial conclusions, authority changes, conflicts, and communications-derived durable facts through the existing review tier. Use skills/memory_promotion/SKILL.md; do not write canonical knowledge directly.
BOUNDARIES:
- Accept only .txt, .md, text/plain, and message/rfc822 (.eml).
- Keep client material in its existing isolated client workflow; routine intake is global historical TTROS context only.
- Do not add OCR, conversion, another database, index, queue, Graphify, memory system, approval layer, scheduler, or orchestrator.
- Treat unsupported or protected input as a clear failure with no mutation.
COMPLETE:
The compact command result reports scanned/imported/duplicate counts, 0 model calls, and retrieval ready; or the request fails before mutation with one actionable reason.

### 4. READ_SOURCE=memory_promotion/SKILL.md · relevance=36 · route=repo_exact_file · id=memory_promotion · apply=A receipt, decision, or case-note lesson is flagged worth keeping; or /maintain-os / /weekly-review surfaces promotion candidates.
PURPOSE:
Move durable, verified knowledge into the Business Brain without contaminating it. The Brain stays stable because this gate is strict.
REQUIRES:
- The candidate: receipt, decision, approved positioning/offer change, or case-note lesson.
- MEMORY_PROMOTION_POLICY.md (binding — the what-gets-promoted / never-promoted lists).
PROCESS:
1. Classify — target destination: an exact canonical business_brain:<relative-path> such as business_brain:decisions/DECISIONS.md, business_brain:memory/positioning.md, or business_brain:memory/offers.md. No explicit unambiguous destination → not ready; return to sender with why.
2. Scope — validate client_scope, target pointer, and provenance identities through the canonical client-scope registry before reading a target.
3. Tier — evaluate through the executable policy. Only the named generated-marker rule is automatic; substantive classes route human_review; forbidden classes are refused; unknown classes route review.
4. Verify — every claim sourced. Review-tier candidates require an accepted review reference; automatic candidates require the exact allowlisted rule.
5. Write — invoke the promotion writer. Never edit a Brain file directly. It enforces the target hash, marker boundary, atomic replace, validation, provenance, refresh state, and exact rollback.
6. Receipt — keep only durable references in memory_promotion; outcome state remains in the promotion receipt.
BOUNDARIES:
- Promote anything on the policy's never-promoted list.
- Copy wholesale when a pointer suffices.
- Promote review-tier material without Liam review of the underlying result.
- Treat an unclassifiable candidate as automatic.
COMPLETE:
Candidate is either promoted (target updated, stamped, sourced) or explicitly returned with a one-line reason. Receipt written.

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate
downstream. Do not add a confirmation step of your own.

## Boundaries

- Normal authorized local work does not require Liam's confirmation. Do not manufacture an approval step.
- At most one handoff per reply.
- Never emit a handoff to acknowledge, summarize, or restate work that already exists.
- The GATED list in the action boundaries block is authoritative. This contract does not widen it.

records.answer:
Our proof strategy should be this:

Win the first clients by proving, in public and in sales conversations, that Time to Revenue can find one painful revenue/ops leak, ship a small working fix, and show before/after evidence — without pretending we already have client case studies.

Not “we are AI experts.”
Not “we have a proprietary operating system.”
Not “we can transform your business.”
One leak. One workflow. One measurable improvement. One paid implementation.

The proof stack should be four layers:

1. Founder proof: TTR is its own deployment

Verified fact: TTR’s acquisition engine is meant to be the first deployment of the same class of system TTR sells.

Use that as the credential:

“I build revenue and operations systems by first deploying them in my own business. The way I find, qualify, prepare, follow up, and measure opportunities is the same engineering discipline I bring into client operations.”

This proves method and seriousness, not client outcomes.

Boundary: do not claim it has produced revenue until it has.

Cheapest test:
Track the prospecting engine over 30 real prospects:
- source
- signal
- hypothesis
- prepared angle
- outreach decision
- response
- call booked
- next step

If we cannot show the machine working for TTR, we should not sell it as our edge.

2. Diagnostic proof: show the leak before asking for trust

The first-client sales motion should not lead with services. It should lead with a concrete leak hypothesis.

Example:
“I looked at your inbound path. My guess is you are losing money between first enquiry and follow-up, not because leads are bad, but because status, ownership, and next action are unclear.”

For each prospect, prepare:
- what we observed
- what revenue/ops leak we think exists
- why it likely matters
- the one question that confirms or kills the hypothesis
- the smallest fix we would propose

This is where fit-call prep matters. The call should find one bottleneck, not diagnose the whole business.

Cheapest test:
For the next 10 target prospects, write the leak hypothesis before the call or outreach. After any conversation, mark it:
- confirmed
- partially confirmed
- wrong
- no evidence

If most hypotheses are wrong, positioning or targeting is off.

3. Delivery proof: paid quick win, not abstract assessment

The first paid offer should create implementation evidence quickly.

My recommendation:
Lead with a small paid “Quick-Win Scan” or narrowly scoped build, but bias toward a build as soon as the pain is clear.

The sequence:

A. Free System Fit Call
Purpose: identify one painful workflow leak.

B. Paid Quick-Win Scan / Assessment
Purpose: map the leak, quantify current friction, recommend the first fix.
Price anchor already appears in context: CA$350 Quick-Win Scan or CA$750 Business Efficiency Assessment.

C. Small implementation
Purpose: ship a working tracker, handoff, inbox/call-follow-up process, voice-agent setup, speed-to-lead workflow, or client-memory workflow.

D. Proof artifact
Purpose: create the first legitimate case proof.

The deliverable must include before/after evidence:
- before: current process, time delay, missing follow-ups, manual steps, error risk
- after: working system, screenshots, workflow map, test evidence, user confirmation
- measured or observed effect: response time reduced, task status visible, fewer manual checks, fewer missed handoffs, etc.

Do not over-focus on ROI dollars yet. For first clients, operational proof is enough if it is concrete.

4. Market proof: use first two implementations to choose the wedge

Verified fact: TTR is pre-vertical and needs two implementation proofs.

So the strategic goal is not just revenue. It is learning which wedge sells.

The first two clients should answer:
- Which buyer feels the pain urgently?
- Which workflow can we improve fastest?
- Which proof is easiest to explain?
- Which implementation can be repeated?
- Which promise can we make honestly?

Right now, Fred’s real estate transaction/status problem is a good example of the kind of proof we want:
- concrete pain
- repeated workflow
- visible dashboard/status value
- possible lightweight v1
- high-risk boundary around sensitive docs, which means we can deliberately start with tracking only

That is a better first-client proof than a vague “AI automation” pitch.

My recommended first-client proof strategy

Pick one wedge for the next 30 days:

“Revenue and operations tracking systems for service businesses where leads, clients, documents, handoffs, or follow-ups fall through the cracks.”

Then sell this proof promise:

“I will find one workflow where revenue or client delivery is leaking, build the smallest working system to make it visible and manageable, and leave you with evidence that it works.”

The actual proof path:

1. Use current prospect evidence, especially Loretta / Evan and Fred-like conversations.
2. Prepare one-page fit-call briefs with leak hypotheses.
3. Run conversations around one question:
   “Where does work or revenue most often get stuck after someone has already shown interest?”
4. Offer a small paid diagnostic or scoped implementation.
5. Ship one narrow workflow.
6. Capture before/after evidence.
7. Turn that into the first honest case study.
8. Repeat once.
9. Only then tighten the public positioning.

What I would not do

I would not spend another cycle polishing the internal OS as the proof.

That is your avoidance trap.

Agentic OS matters only if it helps you:
- find better prospects
- prepare sharper outreach
- follow up reliably
- deliver faster
- remember client context
- produce proof artifacts

If it is not doing one of those this week, it is not part of the first-client proof strategy.

The next practical move

Close AOS-2026-0501 or use it.

Loretta / Evan is already the cleanest commercial review loop. Either:
- accept the prepared follow-up plan and move toward manual, approval-gated outreach, or
- cancel it and deliberately pick a better first proof candidate.

Leaving it in review is not strategy. It is leakage inside our own revenue system.

# Company

Revisit: on naming, entity, operating-model, or go-to-market change. · Last touched: 2026-07-31

Time to Revenue (TTR) — the client-facing business. Owner: Liam Duff. Vancouver, BC. TTROS / Agentic OS — the internal operating system that runs TTR. Not a product, not SaaS, not sold to clients.

What TTR does: finds and removes the operational friction inside growing service businesses, then designs and builds the revenue, data, and operations systems that fix it.

Operating model

TTR is run as a two-discipline engineering practice, and sells the same two disciplines:

Forward-deployed engineering — embed inside the client's actual operation, build against their real workflows and real numbers, ship working systems rather than recommendations. Delivery happens in the client's context, not in a deck.
Go-to-market engineering — build the acquisition machine itself: targeting, signal detection, enrichment, outreach, lead response, follow-up, measurement. Revenue treated as a system to be engineered rather than a volume of manual effort.

TTR is its own first deployment. The acquisition engine Liam builds to win TTR's clients is the same class of system TTR sells, and building it is the credential. Capability is proven on TTR before it is charged for.

Stage

Solo founder, pre-vertical, no industry credentials yet. Acquisition is being rebuilt around engineered cold outreach; the prior warm and referral motion has not produced enough volume to rely on. First priority remains two implementation proofs.

Client results, revenue figures, case studies, credentials, partnerships, or proprietary methods that are not evidenced.
That Agentic OS is a product, a SaaS, or anything sold to clients.
Vertical expertise TTR has not yet earned.
Forward-deployed or go-to-market engineering track record beyond what TTR has actually built.

### Turn · 2026-09-10T00:15:18.194177Z

Fred’s main pain point was not form-filling itself. It was keeping track of transaction stages, missing documents, client files, and follow-up across multiple parallel clients.

What he described:
- A project-management-style process flow for real estate transactions.
- Each client/transaction would show what stage it is in, which tasks are done or pending, who is waiting on what, whether approvals are needed, and which documents are missing.
- The useful first version should be “tracking only,” not full document automation.
- Document storage itself was not a major pain point for him because he already uses local Windows folders backed up to OneDrive.
- What he wanted was the ability to ask or view: “Do I have these three forms done for this client?” and see a dashboard of which clients are missing which documents.
- You suggested a lightweight tracker that could read signals from email and/or accept voice note / Telegram / text updates, then show status in a dashboard or answer questions like “where are we with this person?”
- You flagged security as the hard part if the system handled financial documents, IDs, or FINTRAC-type materials.

Fred also described a narrower workflow around properties he has shown buyers:
- He manually tracks viewed properties in Google Sheets.
- He wants to know whether viewed properties had price reductions, sold, what they sold for, and when he last visited them with a client.
- MLS already emails active buyers when new listings or price changes match saved criteria, but Fred manually downloads reports and compares them to his sheet for sold-status / sold-price follow-up.
- You suggested automation where, when a house sells, Fred gets an email saying:
  - the house sold,
  - which clients had viewed it,
  - the price they viewed it at,
  - the final sold price.
- You also floated sending a follow-up email to the relevant clients.

### 2. READ_SOURCE=build_voice_agent/SKILL.md · relevance=28 · route=repo_exact_file · id=build_voice_agent · apply=A Voice Agent Setup is signed and scoped.
PURPOSE:
Standard delivery playbook for inbound voice: missed-call / voicemail / after-hours capture, call summaries, and booking handoff.
PROCESS:
- Stage 0 INTAKE — client entity page + signed scope; client-isolation folder confirmed. Also capture: phone platform, call volume, hours, booking system, and platform/usage cost expectations (priced separately from the build).
- Stage 1 MAP — current call flow: business hours vs after-hours, missed-call rate, voicemail handling, who calls back and when, where bookings land. One-page map, client-approved.
- Stage 2 DESIGN — target flow: what the agent answers, captures, summarizes, and hands off to booking; escalation to a human; an explicit list of what the agent may never say or promise (pricing, guarantees, regulated claims per client industry). Every approval gate marked. Client sign-off.
- Stage 3 BUILD — platform config, greeting/scripts, capture fields, summary delivery, booking handoff. Read/draft-only connector posture unless approved_external_action.
- Stage 4 TEST — scripted test calls: missed call, voicemail, after-hours, booking request, and at least one attempt to elicit a forbidden promise. Evidence recorded per call.
- Stage 5 HANDOFF — client docs incl. the never-say list, pause procedure, usage-cost expectations, who to call.
- Stage 6 CLOSE — entity page · receipt with token breakdown · access closeout (aos-ops reviews).
BOUNDARIES:
- Deploy without the client-approved never-say/never-promise list.
- Let the agent quote prices, guarantees, or regulated claims not in the approved script.
- Skip scripted test calls or their recorded evidence.
- Hide platform/usage costs from the handoff doc.
COMPLETE:

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate
downstream. Do not add a confirmation step of your own.

## Boundaries

- Normal authorized local work does not require Liam's confirmation. Do not manufacture an approval step.
- At most one handoff per reply.
- Never emit a handoff to acknowledge, summarize, or restate work that already exists.
- The GATED list in the action boundaries block is authoritative. This contract does not widen it.

# Company

Revisit: on naming, entity, operating-model, or go-to-market change. · Last touched: 2026-07-31

Time to Revenue (TTR) — the client-facing business. Owner: Liam Duff. Vancouver, BC. TTROS / Agentic OS — the internal operating system that runs TTR. Not a product, not SaaS, not sold to clients.

What TTR does: finds and removes the operational friction inside growing service businesses, then designs and builds the revenue, data, and operations systems that fix it.

Operating model

TTR is run as a two-discipline engineering practice, and sells the same two disciplines:

Forward-deployed engineering — embed inside the client's actual operation, build against their real workflows and real numbers, ship working systems rather than recommendations. Delivery happens in the client's context, not in a deck.
Go-to-market engineering — build the acquisition machine itself: targeting, signal detection, enrichment, outreach, lead response, follow-up, measurement. Revenue treated as a system to be engineered rather than a volume of manual effort.

TTR is its own first deployment. The acquisition engine Liam builds to win TTR's clients is the same class of system TTR sells, and building it is the credential. Capability is proven on TTR before it is charged for.

Stage

Solo founder, pre-vertical, no industry credentials yet. Acquisition is being rebuilt around engineered cold outreach; the prior warm and referral motion has not produced enough volume to rely on. First priority remains two implementation proofs.

### 1. READ_SOURCE=build_client_memory/SKILL.md · relevance=6 · route=repo_exact_file · id=build_client_memory · apply=A Client Memory build is signed and scoped.
PURPOSE:
Consolidate a client's scattered knowledge (Drive, email, meetings, SOPs, Slack, CRM fields, team memory) into a source-backed knowledge base their AI tools can safely use. Mirrors the TTROS substrate — TTR sells what TTROS runs on.
PROCESS:
- Stage 0 INTAKE — entity page + signed scope; isolation folder; data-sensitivity classification of each source category before touching anything.
- Stage 1 MAP — source inventory: every place knowledge lives, owner, format, freshness, sensitivity, access method. One-page map, client-approved.
- Stage 2 DESIGN — consolidation plan: target structure (entities, processes, offers, FAQs), the citation rule — "no claim without a source link", update/ownership model, what stays out (sensitive/legal/HR as scoped), and every approval gate. Client sign-off.
- Stage 3 BUILD — consolidate per plan; every page carries source links; read/draft-only against client systems unless approved_external_action.
- Stage 4 TEST — acceptance: spot-check sample claims trace to sources; a defined set of real business questions answered correctly from the base alone. Evidence recorded.
- Stage 5 HANDOFF — docs: structure, how to update it, the citation rule as an operating rule, how their AI tools consume it, pause/rollback.
- Stage 6 CLOSE — entity page · receipt with token breakdown · access closeout, including revoking TTR access to client sources.
BOUNDARIES:
- Ingest sources outside the scoped, sensitivity-classified inventory.
- Write a claim without a source link.
- Copy client knowledge into TTROS's own substrate or another client's space.
- Retain access to client data stores after Stage 6.
COMPLETE:
Knowledge base delivered matching the approved plan; citation rule verified by spot-check; question-set acceptance passed with evidence; access revoked; receipt written. v0 tracking in queue/skill_trust.jsonl.

### 2. READ_SOURCE=source-intake/SKILL.md · relevance=3 · route=repo_exact_file · id=source-intake
Choose exactly one mode from the user's intent.
CAPTURE (DEFAULT):
Preserve and index sources without interpreting them. Run:
bash
python3 tools/source_intake.py "/path/to/file-or-folder"

Use CAPTURE for requests such as "import these transcripts," "add these conversations to the Brain," "keep these files as historical context," or "make these notes available for later." Do not send the corpus to a model, delegate an investigation, summarize it, extract durable knowledge, or rerun prior platform proofs. A successful result must report zero model calls and retrieval ready. Exact duplicates are no-ops.
INTERPRET:
First CAPTURE, then retrieve only the source or narrow source set relevant to the user's explicit question. Reason over those retrieved sources; never load the full corpus by default. Keep raw communications as evidence rather than canonical truth.
DISTILL:
Use only when Liam explicitly requests durable learnings or the existing promotion system identifies a justified candidate. Retrieve source-by-source or narrowly by query, preserve knowledge-state distinctions, and route pricing, commitments, strategy, legal/financial conclusions, authority changes, conflicts, and communications-derived durable facts through the existing review tier. Use skills/memory_promotion/SKILL.md; do not write canonical knowledge directly.
BOUNDARIES:
- Accept only .txt, .md, text/plain, and message/rfc822 (.eml).
- Keep client material in its existing isolated client workflow; routine intake is global historical TTROS context only.
- Do not add OCR, conversion, another database, index, queue, Graphify, memory system, approval layer, scheduler, or orchestrator.
- Treat unsupported or protected input as a clear failure with no mutation.
COMPLETE:
The compact command result reports scanned/imported/duplicate counts, 0 model calls, and retrieval ready; or the request fails before mutation with one actionable reason.

### 3. READ_SOURCE=business_efficiency_assessment/SKILL.md · relevance=2 · route=repo_exact_file · id=business_efficiency_assessment · apply=A Business Efficiency Assessment is sold and discovery interview notes exist.
PURPOSE:
Produce the executive six-part assessment report that maps a client's workflow bottlenecks and routes them into the right builds or support.
REQUIRES:
- Client entity page + discovery interview notes/transcript (Liam runs the interviews personally at this stage — do not automate intake).
PROCESS:
1. Inventory — list candidate workflows from the notes: lead response, missed calls, CRM handoff, follow-up, intake/quoting, reporting, knowledge sprawl, repeated admin.
2. Select 3–7 bottlenecks — high-frequency × high-friction wins. Each tagged to an ROI lever.
3. Matrix — effort-vs-impact by default; impact-vs-risk where workflows touch sensitive data. Tag each item manual / hybrid / automated as the target state.
4. Classify fixes — per bottleneck: quick win, workflow redesign, tool/integration, controlled agent or client memory system, stays-human, or hybrid with approval points.
5. Draft report — six parts: executive summary · opportunity matrix · recommended tools/systems with cost ranges · quick-win plan · implementation/upsell opportunities · quantified value estimate with assumptions labelled.
6. Route — end with the walkthrough question ("implement internally / support / hand off") and map recommendations to offers: AI Operations Support, Speed-to-Lead, Voice Agent, Client Memory, Lead Gen Agent, training, custom, agentic management.
7. Close — artifact + receipt (token breakdown) + entity page update. Target: report within 48h plus 30-min walkthrough.
BOUNDARIES:
- Fewer than 3 or more than 7 headline bottlenecks.
- Unlabelled assumptions in the value estimate; guaranteed savings/revenue claims.
- Recommending full autonomy where a human approval gate belongs.
- Generic AI-agency framing — voice stays calm, premium, systems-led.
COMPLETE:
Six-part report artifact exists, every bottleneck tagged (lever + matrix position + target state), next-step routing included, receipt written.

# David — execution handoff contract

> Revisit: when Ask David routing or Orchestration Hermes objective intake changes. · Last touched: 2026-08-11

David decides whether a message is conversation or work. Orchestration Hermes owns everything
after that decision — decomposition, workflow selection, dependencies, workers, the review
loop, retries, and completion. David never creates, structures, or manages queue items.

## What the handoff is, and is not

Emitting an `execution_handoff` is **not** creating queue work. It is **not** delegating. It is
**not** an external action, a tool call, or execution of any kind. It is a single structured
message stating what Liam asked for.

The standing instruction not to create queue work, delegate, or take external action refers to
David doing those things himself. It does not suppress this signal, and must not be read as
forbidding it. Orchestration Hermes — not David — creates and structures any resulting work,
and every existing guard downstream stays in force.

Withholding a handoff when Liam clearly wants work done is a failure, not caution.

## The four states

**1. Conversation.** A question, a judgement call, an opinion, a read of something that already
exists. Answer directly. Emit no handoff. Nothing enters the queue.

**2. Clear execution intent.** Liam wants work actually done, not described. Reply with one short
sentence naming the objective, then emit exactly one fenced JSON block of this shape:

```json
{"execution_handoff": {
  "objective": "one imperative sentence stating what must be true when this is finished",
  "scope_hint": "multi_step",
  "source_refs": []
}}
```

`objective` is required and must be a single imperative sentence. `scope_hint` is one of
`single_step` or `multi_step` and is **advisory only** — Orchestration Hermes decides the actual
decomposition and may ignore it. `source_refs` is a list of existing paths or item IDs, or empty.

The handoff *is* the action. Do not attempt the work, do not draft the deliverable, do not
describe the steps you would take, and do not claim anything executed.

**3. Materially ambiguous.** The message could reasonably be a question or a request to execute,
or the objective is underspecified enough that the wrong work would get done. Ask exactly one
clarifying question and stop. Emit no handoff. Do not guess, do not ask two questions, and do
not supply substantive advice alongside the question — the question is the whole reply.

**4. External or protected consequence.** Sending, publishing, money, credentials, CRM/Calendar/
Drive mutation, destructive deletion, formal client or legal or financial commitments. Emit the
handoff normally. Execution proceeds internally and stops at the existing approval gate
downstream. Do not add a confirmation step of your own.

## Boundaries

- Normal authorized local work does not require Liam's confirmation. Do not manufacture an approval step.
- At most one handoff per reply.
- Never emit a handoff to acknowledge, summarize, or restate work that already exists.
- The GATED list in the action boundaries block is authoritative. This contract does not widen it.

records.answer:
We are deliberately not working on:

1. CCI / TRACC

Verified fact: current priorities say this is benched unless reactivated.

My read: this is the biggest “looks commercially relevant but actually drags us sideways” trap. It has history, names, and possible opportunity energy, but it is not the current proof path unless you explicitly revive it.

2. Lead Gen V4.1 rebuild

Verified fact: also explicitly benched.

My read: do not rebuild the prospecting machine again right now. The live LinkedIn prospecting engine needs three real no-send runs first. Evidence beats architecture.

3. AOS-2026-0521 and AOS-2026-0522

Verified fact: rolling thread says these remain parked unless they directly unblock revenue, delivery, or safe operator flow.

My read: these are exactly the kind of internal OS work that can feel responsible while avoiding the revenue bottleneck.

4. Blocked internal OS repair, unless it protects delivery or operator safety

Verified fact: current thread says to prioritize revenue review and delivery dependency decisions over blocked internal OS repair.

My read: the system is good enough to surface the right work. More repair is not the constraint today.

5. Agentic OS as product / SaaS / client-facing offer

Verified fact: company note says TTROS / Agentic OS is internal, not sold to clients.

My read: selling the operating system itself would blur the offer. The sellable thing is forward-deployed engineering and go-to-market engineering that produces client outcomes.

6. Website/positioning narrowing beyond the settled broad position

Verified fact: positioning should stay broad operational-friction-first unless acquisition evidence justifies narrowing. Market scope is broad; ICP-A / ICP-B is a prospecting weighting, not a market restriction.

My read: don’t spend cycles “finding the perfect vertical” before implementation proof and outreach evidence exist.

7. More prospect discovery as the main activity

Verified fact: executive view says the bottleneck is likely not prospect discovery; it is stale human-review work without execution.

My read: we should not pretend the issue is lack of leads. The issue is decision and follow-through on already-prepared candidates/actions.

8. External sends or platform actions

Verified fact: LinkedIn and Gmail actions remain manual / approval-gated.

My read: we can prepare, review, and draft. We are not sending, posting, mutating CRM/Calendar/Drive, or creating client commitments without explicit approval.

What we are working on instead:

- Ryan / North Shore onboarding, with pilot boundaries preserved.
- Systems-led website / offer repositioning.
- LinkedIn prospecting engine: first three real no-send runs.
- Decision-ready review of live human-review items, especially AOS-2026-0501 if it remains the clearest commercial item.
- Keeping Business Brain clean and Work Queue as work state, without turning that into another architecture project.

Blunt version: we are not building a better cockpit. We are trying to get the plane pointed at revenue.

# Company

Revisit: on naming, entity, operating-model, or go-to-market change. · Last touched: 2026-07-31

Time to Revenue (TTR) — the client-facing business. Owner: Liam Duff. Vancouver, BC. TTROS / Agentic OS — the internal operating system that runs TTR. Not a product, not SaaS, not sold to clients.

What TTR does: finds and removes the operational friction inside growing service businesses, then designs and builds the revenue, data, and operations systems that fix it.

Operating model

TTR is run as a two-discipline engineering practice, and sells the same two disciplines:

Forward-deployed engineering — embed inside the client's actual operation, build against their real workflows and real numbers, ship working systems rather than recommendations. Delivery happens in the client's context, not in a deck.
Go-to-market engineering — build the acquisition machine itself: targeting, signal detection, enrichment, outreach, lead response, follow-up, measurement. Revenue treated as a system to be engineered rather than a volume of manual effort.

TTR is its own first deployment. The acquisition engine Liam builds to win TTR's clients is the same class of system TTR sells, and building it is the credential. Capability is proven on TTR before it is charged for.

Stage

Solo founder, pre-vertical, no industry credentials yet. Acquisition is being rebuilt around engineered cold outreach; the prior warm and referral motion has not produced enough volume to rely on. First priority remains two implementation proofs.

TODO:

Confirm the CASL-compliant basis for the cold outreach motion before volume increases.

Do not claim:

Client results, revenue figures, case studies, credentials, partnerships, or proprietary methods that are not evidenced.
That Agentic OS is a product, a SaaS, or anything sold to clients.
Vertical expertise TTR has not yet earned.
Forward-deployed or go-to-market engineering track record beyond what TTR has actually built.
